Content:
$25 TIX TO WORLD PREMIERE CUBAN DANCE FILM + LIVE PERFORMANCE + PARTY (SPONSORED)
The Essence of Us: A Cuban Story
A World Premiere Film Directed by
Nel Shelby
Featuring
Malpaso Dance Company
and
Pedro Ruiz
With a Live Performance by
Ballet Hispánico New York
Plus afterparty!
An evening celebrating Cuban dance, creative exchange, and the power of artistic connection.
When visa barriers prevented Malpaso Dance Company from traveling to New York for the planned world premiere of Pedro Ruiz’s new work, the project became something equally revealing:
The Essence of Us
, a new documentary following Ruiz’s creative process in Havana, created by acclaimed filmmaker Nel Shelby in collaboration with cinematographer and editor Ashli Bickford.
The program opens with a thrilling live performance by Ballet Hispánico New York featuring works by Cuban and Cuban American choreographers like Eduardo Vilaro and Marianela Boán, and continues with Cuban-inspired music, cocktails, and dancing, as Opening Night spills from the stage into a post-performance party for all.​​

COME SEE THE WORLD PREMIERE OF ISLA (SPONSORED)
ISLA
, the latest full-length work from acclaimed theater company
Hit the Lights!
, is a uniquely original family history led by founding company member Samantha Blain. In her Caribbean coming-of-age story, Blain’s American lineage is born when three young women learn that
sometimes the real world can be stronger than magic
.
Based on the true saga of one family exodus to Miami via the 1960’s Freedom Flights,
ISLA
is a visually sumptuous, musically driven play that evokes the rustic spirit of pre-Castro Cuba’s kitchens, fields, dance halls and public squares. Blain, in the role of her aunt, must ally with her sisters to chart a path to an uncertain and newly imagined future.
Every performance features a
full original songbook and a live Latin jazz-influenced score
. Cinematic projections, recorded interviews with Blain’s mother and aunts, and an extended cast of handmade shadow puppets revitalize this carousel slideshow of generational memory through the exquisite craft of HTL’s technical team.
ISLA
is an intergenerational experience.
Bring the whole family.

.

A $30 EXISTENTIAL CRISIS: FUNERAL OF GOD COMES TO HELL’S KITCHEN (SPONSORED)
Certainty has enjoyed a very long run. Now a theatre company has been asked to give it a proper sendoff.
Funeral of god
, the new play by award-winning playwright Brian S. Brijbag, makes its world premiere at the Broadway Bound Theatre Festival. In this absurdist dark comedy, four members of a theatre company attempt the impossible: staging a funeral for god. Rehearsal soon becomes a philosophical labor dispute involving belief, grief, ritual, responsibility, and the inconvenient fact that nobody agrees on what the ceremony is for.
No deity is scheduled for burial. This is theatre, where the dead arrive on cue, the living ask for notes, and certainty has neglected to learn its lines.
Sharp, strange, and unexpectedly tender,
Funeral of god
asks what remains when the old answers stop answering. It plays four performances only at AMT Theater in Hell’s Kitchen. Tickets start at $30, a modest price for an evening spent inspecting the foundations of existence.
Thursday, July 30 at 5 PM
Friday, July 31 at 8 PM
Saturday, August 1 at 2 PM
Sunday, August 2 at 2 PM, followed by a talkback

Title: FIVE DECADES OF BLACK DANCE EXCELLENCE, LIVE AT THE JOYCE (SPONSORED)

Content:
FIVE DECADES OF BLACK DANCE EXCELLENCE, LIVE AT THE JOYCE (SPONSORED)
For more than fifty-six years,
PHILADANCO!
has stood among the most influential forces in American concert dance — producing generations of technically extraordinary artists while preserving and advancing the traditions of Black American concert dance at the highest level.
This July, the internationally celebrated company returns to
The Joyce Theater
fresh off a three-week European tour, bringing New York a program that honors its legacy while pushing boldly into the future.
Four distinctive voices. One unforgettable week.
The engagement features two New York premieres —
Thang Dao
‘s striking
Without Witness
and
Tommie-Waheed Evans
‘ emotionally charged
Promise Me You Won’t Call
— alongside a major new creation from
Rennie Harris
, set to the unmistakable sound of Philadelphia International Records.
By popular demand, the run also marks the
25th anniversary revival of Christopher Huggins
‘
Enemy Behind the Gates
, an epic tour de force that has endured across generations and continues to resonate with audiences worldwide.
Whether you’ve followed PHILADANCO! since Joan Myers Brown founded the company in 1970, or you’re discovering their unmatched technique for the first time, this is a rare convergence of choreographic talent you won’t want to miss — a portrait of a company that continues to set the standard for artistic excellence and cultural impact.
PHILADANCO! at The Joyce Theater
July 29 – August 2
